'''Eurobarometer''' is a series of [[public opinion]] [[statistical survey|surveys]] conducted regularly on behalf of the [[European Commission]] and other [[Institutions of the European Union|EU institutions]] since 1974. These surveys address a wide variety of topical issues relating to the [[European Union]] throughout its [[Member state of the European Union|member states]].

The Eurobarometer results are published by the European Commission's [[Directorate-General Communication (European Commission)|Directorate-General Communication]]. Its database since 1974 is one of the largest in the world.<ref>{{Cite web |title=GESIS - Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences |url=https://www.gesis.org/en/eurobarometer-data-service/data-and-documentation/publications |access-date=2024-12-13 |website=www.gesis.org |language=en}}</ref>

==History==
In 1970 and 1971, the [[European Commission]] conducted surveys in the six member countries (at that time) of the [[European Community]]—Belgium, France, [[West Germany]], Italy, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands. These surveys assessed public opinion on individual national priorities as well as integrated European functions and organisations, including the [[European Economic Community|Common Market]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eurobarometer |url=https://europa.eu/eurobarometer/about/eurobarometer |access-date=2024-12-13 |website=europa.eu}}</ref>

Regular semi-annual polls of member nations – now also including [[Denmark]], [[Ireland]] and the [[United Kingdom]] – began in September 1973, with the survey series first being given the name [[Eurobarometer]] in 1974. The fieldwork for Euro-Barometer 1 was conducted in April–May of that year, with results published in July.<ref>{{cite web |title=Standard Eurobarometer 1 - Spring 1974 |url=https://europa.eu/eurobarometer/surveys/detail/1459 |access-date=2025-08-24 |publisher=European Commission}}</ref>

A first international survey on attitudes towards European unification was carried out in 1962 at the request of the Press and Information Service of the European Communities in Belgium, France, [[West Germany]], Italy, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands.<ref>{{cite web |title=Attitudes towards Europe (1962) |url=https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA0078 |access-date=2025-08-24 |publisher=GESIS – Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences}}</ref>

== Surveys ==

* '''Standard Eurobarometer''': Regular public opinion surveys conducted by the European Commission since 1974, assessing EU citizens' views on various topics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Standard Eurobarometer 103 - Spring 2025 |url=https://europa.eu/eurobarometer/surveys/detail/3372 |access-date=2025-08-24 |publisher=European Commission}}</ref>
* '''Flash Eurobarometer''': Ad-hoc thematic surveys carried out within a short timespan on specific topics relevant to EU policies.<ref>{{cite web |title=About Eurobarometer |url=https://europa.eu/eurobarometer/about/eurobarometer |access-date=2025-08-24 |publisher=European Commission}}</ref>
* '''Central and Eastern Eurobarometer''': Annual surveys conducted between 1990 and 1997 in up to 20 Central and Eastern European countries, monitoring economic and political changes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Central and Eastern Eurobarometer |url=https://europa.eu/eurobarometer/surveys/browse/all/series/188225 |access-date=2025-08-24 |publisher=European Commission}}</ref>
* '''Candidate Countries Eurobarometer''': Surveys launched in 2001 for EU applicant states, later merged into the Standard series. As of 2024, includes data from Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Turkey, the Turkish Cypriot Community, and the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web |title=Candidate Countries Eurobarometer |url=https://europa.eu/eurobarometer/surveys/browse/all/series/300602 |access-date=2025-08-24 |publisher=European Commission}}</ref><ref>{{cite report |url=https://europa.eu/eurobarometer/api/deliverable/download/file?deliverableId=95656 |title=Standard Eurobarometer 102 – Autumn 2024 – Annex |author=<!-- not stated --> |date=November 2024 |publisher=European Commission |doi=10.2775/6217228 |isbn=978-92-68-21830-3 |issn=1977-3927 |access-date=2025-01-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241216061451/https://europa.eu/eurobarometer/api/deliverable/download/file?deliverableId=95656 |archive-date=2024-12-16 |format=PDF |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Controversies ==
In August 2025, Dutch research uncovered widespread sampling errors by Verian, the polling firm that conducts Eurobarometer surveys in the Netherlands. It found that in the samples in the Netherlands, Sweden, and Finland, people with a progressive left political preference and a higher level of education are overrepresented. Both these traits are correlated with pro-EU preferences.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maurice |date=2025-08-03 |title=Hoe de Eurobarometer systematisch een te positieve mening over de EU laat zien |url=https://maurice.nl/2025/08/03/eurobarometer-positief/ |access-date=2025-11-21 |website=Maurice de Hond |language=nl-NL}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Maurice |date=2025-11-20 |title=Eurobarometer blijft fouten stijfkoppig maken |url=https://maurice.nl/2025/11/20/eurobarometer-blijft-fouten-stijfkoppig-maken/ |access-date=2025-11-21 |website=Maurice de Hond |language=nl-NL}}</ref>
